correction.text: valid for 1521-1523 (Sweden contested)

keyframe_review.note: 1,285,990 km2, the whole realm to 1525. The Swedish War of Liberation began in January 1521; Gustav Vasa was recognised leader at Vadstena in August 1521; Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523, Gustav was proclaimed king on 6 June 1523 and Stockholm was taken on 17 June 1523. So the shape stands for 1521-1523 with Sweden a contested zone, and the union ends in June 1523, not 1525; Denmark and Norway continue as Denmark-Norway (infobox 'established: 1523') and Sweden is independent.

region.text: the three kingdoms under one monarch

ledger.note: 17 June 1397: the Kalmar Union is proclaimed. The infobox reads 'Inception: 17 June 1397' and the Eric of Pomerania page: 'On 17 June 1397, he was crowned king of the three Nordic countries in the cathedral of Kalmar'; Margaret 'remained the de facto ruler of the three kingdoms until her death in 1412'.

1408: the Teutonic Order sells Gotland to Denmark. State page: 'Gotland | 1398-1408'; 'Letzkau arranged that the Order sell Gotland to Denmark'. Counterpart is the Order; the page does not name the buyer's ruler.

1426: war with Holstein and the Hanseatic League begins. 'From 1426 to 1435, he was at war with the German Hanseatic League and Holstein.' The page gives no 1409 start for the Schleswig dispute and does not say which campaign first took ground.

region.text: the western Greenland cells in Cliopatria's 1402 shape

ledger.note: 1429: Cliopatria drops the Greenland cells from the union's shape. The page's footnote says 'No direct contact took place between Greenland and the Kalmar Union during the latter's existence'; no page opened dates any Greenland event, so this records Cliopatria's change only.
17 July 1435: the Peace of Vordingborg ends the Holstein war. 'On 17 July 1435, he signed the Peace of Vordingborg' with the Hanseatic League and Holstein.

17 July 1435: Schleswig passes to the count of Holstein. 'Under the 1435 treaty, the Duchy of Schleswig was ceded to the count of Holstein'; the war 'led to the loss of the South Jutlandic areas that he had already obtained'. Cliopatria keeps part of Schleswig in the union to 1458.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 20 June 1448: Sweden elects its own king, Karl Knutsson, and the union is broken. 'Karl was elected king of Sweden on 20 June, and on 28 June, he was hailed as the new monarch at the Stones of Mora'; the Kalmar page: 'Christopher's death in 1448 ended a period of uninterrupted union' and Karl ruled Sweden in 1448-1457.

1 September 1448: the House of Oldenburg takes the Danish throne. 'Count Christian was elected at Viborg on 1 September 1448'; he ruled Denmark 1448-1481, Norway 1450-1481 and Sweden 1457-1464 (Kalmar page). Cliopatria's 'House of Oldenburg' row (1450-1458) is this dynasty's rule in the union's realm.

February 1449: Norway splits between Christian and Karl Knutsson. 'In February 1449 part of the Norwegian council backed Karl. On 15 June 1449 another group paid homage to Christian, and on 20 November 1449 Karl was crowned in Trondheim.'

August 1450: Christian is crowned king of Norway. 'In June 1450 the Swedish council forced Karl to renounce his claim on Norway. Christian was crowned king of Norway in Trondheim on 2 August 1450'; the Treaty of Bergen of 29 August 1450 was a Denmark-Norway union treaty.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 23 June 1457: Christian I becomes king of Sweden. The infobox dates his Swedish reign from 23 June 1457, with the coronation at Uppsala on 29 June 1457, after Karl Knutsson 'was driven into exile in 1457'.

region.text: the Duchy of Schleswig and the County of Holstein-Rendsburg

ledger.note: 5 March 1460: Christian I is confirmed Duke of Schleswig and Count of Holstein. 'The Estates confirmed Christian's succession at Ribe on 5 March 1460. He then became Duke of Schleswig and Count of Holstein-Rendsburg in 1460' after Adolphus VIII died on 4 December 1459 without heirs.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 23 June 1464: Christian I loses Sweden. His Swedish reign 'ended in 1464 when Kettil Karlsson Vasa' was installed as regent (infobox: 23 June 1464); Karl Knutsson ruled again from 9 August 1464 (Charles VIII page).

1472: Scotland annexes Orkney and Shetland. 'Christian I pledged the islands as security for his daughter's dowry, which was tied to her 1468 betrothal to James III. Scotland annexed the islands in 1472'; a footnote gives 1470 for the transfer.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: 6 October 1497: Hans wins Sweden. 'On 28 September 1497, Hans's army decisively defeated Sten's peasant levy from Dalarna at the Battle of Rotebro. On 6 October, a settlement was reached in Klara Priory, and Sten formally recognized Hans as king and relinquished his regency'; Hans was crowned in Stockholm five days after entering it.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: August 1501: Sweden renounces Hans. 'In August, Sten Sture, Hemming Gadh, and several other members of the Swedish council renounced their allegiance to Hans' (the Kalmar page: Sture became regent again in 1501). 'Queen Christina surrendered on 5 May 1502' in Stockholm.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: November 1520: Christian II is crowned king of Sweden. His 'third attempt made in 1520' succeeded (Bogesund, 19 January 1520); 'Christian was crowned king of Sweden by Trolle in November' (infobox: 4 November 1520, Stockholm), followed by the Stockholm Bloodbath on 8-9 November.

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: January 1521: the Swedish War of Liberation begins. 'The war began in January 1521, when Gustav Vasa was appointed hövitsman (commander) over Dalarna'; he was recognised leader of Sweden at Vadstena in the second half of August 1521, and Christian II's Swedish reign ended on 23 August 1521 (infobox).

region.text: Sweden and southern Finland, the Swedish realm

ledger.note: June 1523: Gustav Vasa takes Stockholm. 'Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523'; 'Gustav Eriksson (Vasa) was proclaimed King of Sweden at the Riksdag in Strängnäs on 6 June 1523'; 'Stockholm was taken on 17 June'. The Danish side kept Blekinge, Skåne and Gotland; the Treaty of Malmö (1 September 1524) formalised the secession.

region.text: the union's three realms: Denmark and Norway continue as Denmark-Norway, Sweden is independent

ledger.note: 6 June 1523: the Kalmar Union ends. 'Gustav Vasa's election as King of Sweden on 6 June 1523 marked Sweden's final secession'; the infobox reads 'Denmark-Norway was established: 1523'; Frederick I renounced his claim to Sweden in 1524 at the Treaty of Malmö. Christian II had been deposed in Denmark on 20 January 1523.

wars.name: War with Holstein and the Hanseatic League (1426-1435)
wars.outcome: Eric lost the South Jutland lands he had won; the Peace of Vordingborg (17 July 1435) ceded Schleswig to the count of Holstein and exempted the Hanseatic cities from the Sound Dues.
wars.note: The page gives no 1409 start for the Schleswig war.

wars.name: Engelbrekt rebellion
wars.outcome: A national and social rebellion of Swedish farmers and mine workers; it led to Eric's overthrow in Denmark and Sweden in 1439 and in Norway in 1442.
wars.note: No territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Contest for Norway between Christian I and Karl Knutsson
wars.outcome: Karl was crowned at Trondheim on 20 November 1449 and forced in June 1450 to renounce Norway; Christian was crowned there on 2 August 1450.
wars.note: A political contest between two elected kings, not a campaign; the page gives no battle.

wars.name: Battle of Brunkeberg
wars.outcome: Christian's 'final attempt to regain Sweden ended in total military failure at the Battle of Brunkeberg (outside Stockholm) October 1471' against Sten Sture the Elder.
wars.note: Sweden stayed out of the union until Hans in 1497.

wars.name: Hans's conquest of Sweden
wars.outcome: Rotebro (28 September 1497), the settlement at Klara Priory (6 October) and Hans's entry into Stockholm: Sten Sture relinquished the regency.
wars.note: The page gives no exact coronation date.

wars.name: Swedish revolt against Hans
wars.outcome: Sture and the council renounced allegiance in August 1501; Queen Christina surrendered Stockholm on 5 May 1502.
wars.note: Hans returned in early 1501 after an eighteen-month absence.

wars.name: War of Hans against Sweden and Lübeck
wars.outcome: 'Between 1510 and 1512, the king waged a final war with both Sweden and Lübeck'; no territorial result is stated.
wars.note: Mentioned in a sentence; the page gives no outcome.

wars.name: Christian II's wars with Sten Sture the Younger
wars.outcome: Failures in 1517 (Vedila) and 1518 (Brännkyrka); in 1520 a large army of French, German and Scottish mercenaries won, Sture was mortally wounded at Bogesund on 19 January 1520 and Christian was crowned in Stockholm in November 1520.
wars.note: The Stockholm Bloodbath was on 8-9 November 1520.

wars.name: Swedish War of Liberation
wars.outcome: Swedish victory: Kalmar fell on 27 May 1523, Gustav Vasa was proclaimed king on 6 June and Stockholm taken on 17 June 1523; the Treaty of Malmö of 1 September 1524 formalised the secession. Lübeck allied with the rebels in 1522.
wars.note: The infobox dates the war 1521-23; Blekinge, Skåne and Gotland stayed Danish.

certainty.note: The union's northern frontiers (Lapland, the Finnish and Karelian marches against Novgorod and Moscow) are approximate throughout and Cliopatria draws Sweden and Finland only in part before 1429; the Danish coasts are firm.

notes: Pages: 8 opened (budget 9, one of them shared with the Teutonic Order dossier). The union is a personal union of three kingdoms. Cliopatria draws it as a territory from 1402 and ends the Old Kingdom of Norway (1401) and Kingdom of Sweden (1401) rows, but keeps Kingdom of Denmark's own row to 1406 (a 72.8 km2 sliver from 1402) and restarts Sweden in 1502; with start 1397 the dossier overlaps those rows in 1397-1401. The Cliopatria row 'House of Oldenburg' (1450-1458) is the Oldenburg kings' rule in the same realm and shares Seshat id sv_kalmar_union; it is merged into this dossier (cliopatria_names; review 2026-10-25): its two shapes are marked wrong with an empty correction (the validator's --resolve warns 'resolves to no cells' twice, intentionally, because the row draws nothing of its own) and its territory is corrected in keyframes 1450-1457; the separate house-of-oldenburg dossier was withdrawn. If the rendering agent wants a separate dynasty colour, the Oldenburg lands would be Norway 1450-1456 and the Swedish realm 1457-1458 and the Kalmar keyframes would have to drop them. The row's 1458 end is Cliopatria's (page silent, confidence 1). A dynasty change inside one state is a rename (here 1 September 1448). Sweden and Finland: the union held them only 1397-1447, June 1457 - June 1464, October 1497 - August 1501 and November 1520 - 1523 (contested from January 1521). Cliopatria draws them in the union all through 1459-1501 and 1521-1525 and has a separate Kingdom of Sweden row only for 1502-1520; the Kingdom of Sweden dossier should draw Sweden for 1448-1457, 1464-1497, 1501-1520 and 1521-1523, and the 1523 end of the union is two years before Cliopatria's 1525. Norway 1449-1450 was contested between Christian I and Karl Knutsson. Denmark-Norway: the Kalmar page's infobox says Denmark-Norway was established in 1523 but Cliopatria's Denmark-Norway row starts in 1526, leaving 1524-1525 undrawn; the Denmark-Norway dossier should start at 1523 or take the Kalmar Union's Danish-Norwegian shape. Schleswig: the 1435 loss and 1460 gain use the counterpart 'Counts of Holstein (Holstein-Rendsburg)', a state with no Cliopatria row; the Holy Roman Empire minor states dossier should cover Holstein. The 1435-1459 Schleswig cut removes all 79 Schleswig cells Cliopatria keeps. Not settled: the 1429 jump in shape and the 1475 Finnish jump (undated), the 1439-1449 Gotland base of the deposed Eric (page gives no dates), the union's capital (undated), a ruler list (none opened), Iceland and the Faroes (no page opened dates anything). The page footnote that Greenland had no contact with the union is the only Greenland statement.
